GoGaming is an e-commerce app that lets users buy gaming products.
Make it simple for users to read trusted reviews and buy products confidently on the go.
To conduct my research, I interviewed five people I play games with.
Persona Jeff. Jeff is a busy gamer and parent who needs a quick way to find durable gaming gear because his young kids wear out equipment fast.
This user journey map shows the path Jeff takes to buy a gaming chair durable enough for his young kids.
Paper wireframes. My goal was to keep the design simple and compact so users could quickly find what they need on a small screen.
Digital wireframes. I added a hamburger menu that users can open and close from any screen. It keeps the layout compact while giving users access to product search options from anywhere in the app.
Digital wireframes. Products show only an image and name, so each listing takes up little space and users can quickly skim to find what they want.
Low-fidelity prototype. The user taps the hamburger menu, selects a product category, chooses a product, then buys it.
I conducted a usability study with five participants of various ages.
Mockups. Based on participant feedback, I switched to a single column and stacked the menu options vertically.
Mockups. Following participant suggestions, I changed the product list from two columns to one and moved the search bar out of the hamburger menu so it’s always visible.
Mockups.
high-fidelity prototype.
Accessibility considerations. Everything users can tap is at least 44 PX. All content sits in a single column. All text have good contrast ratios against its background.
Takeaways. It’s easy to overthink a design for small screens without user feedback.

GoGaming site by Joanna Gohnert
GoGaming is an e-commerce website that lets users buy gaming products.
Make it simple for users to read reviews and buy products with confidence.
To conduct my research, I interviewed people I play games with.
Lukas is a game reviewer and writer who needs a reliable way to verify product reviews so he can be confident in his purchases.
This user journey map follows Lukas as he shops for a headset that meets his gaming and audio needs.
Paper wireframes. My goal was to give users access to high-quality gaming products. I wanted an open layout that lets users see many products on one screen.
Digital wireframes. I wanted a simple but sharp layout that catches users’ attention.
Digital wireframes. For this digital wireframe, I wanted a page where users could see an overview of many products at once.
Low-fidelity prototype. The user searches for a product, selects it, clicks Purchase, enters shipping and card information, then confirms the purchase.
I conducted a usability study on the low-fidelity prototype.
Mockups. My goal was to make actions clearer.
Mockups. I added a back arrow to make navigation easier and a filter button to help users find what they’re looking for.
Mockups.
high-fidelity prototype.

Accessibility considerations. With the site’s bright colors, I made contrast and legibility a priority. I kept the most important actions near the top of each page. The menu changes color on hover, showing users they can interact with it.
Takeaways. There’s a lot I can miss when designing on my own.
